revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Critique the Treasure-Map Plot
revealWordProblem.text: Andrew is reading Captain Vega's treasure map. He needs to plot -3/4 on the number line. He says, "-3/4 has a 3 and a 4, so I start at -3 and count 4 more units to the left, which lands me at -7." Question: Do you agree with where Andrew plotted -3/4? Explain your reasoning and tell exactly where -3/4 belongs on the number line.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: I disagree. -3/4 means three-fourths of one unit, not -3 and then 4 more. It is 3/4 of the way from 0 toward -1, so it belongs between 0 and -1 (a little past the halfway mark). Andrew's point at -7 is far too low; -3/4 = -0.75.

vocabulary.term: Rational Numbers on the Number Line
vocabulary.termEs: Números racionales en la recta numérica
vocabulary.definition: Every rational number has one exact spot on the number line. Writing it as a fraction, a decimal, or an integer does not change where it sits.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cada número racional tiene un lugar exacto en la recta numérica. Escribirlo como fracción, decimal o entero no cambia dónde queda.
vocabulary.visual: −3/2 = −1.5 and 1/2 = 0.5 each sit at one exact point.
vocabulary.cloze: A rational number always has one exact spot on the ___ ___.

examples.why: Its value decides where it goes, not its form.
The digits are not the value — -3/4 is less than one unit from 0.

vocabulary.definition: A number that can be written as a fraction of two integers, with a bottom number that is not zero.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número que se puede escribir como una fracción de dos enteros, con un denominador que no sea cero.
vocabulary.visual: −1/2, 0 and 5/4 each sit at one exact point.
vocabulary.cloze: A number you can write as a fraction of two integers, with a bottom number that is not zero, is a ___.

examples.why: It can be written as −3/1 — both parts are integers.
It can be written as 3/4, so it is rational.

vocabulary.definition: A number that shows part of a whole, like 3/4.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número que muestra una parte de un todo, como 3/4.
vocabulary.visual: 3/4 means 3 out of 4 equal parts — like 3 slices of a pizza cut into 4
vocabulary.cloze: A number that shows part of a whole, like 3/5, is a ___.

examples.text: -3/4 as a point three-quarters of the way from 0 to -1
examples.why: It names a part of a whole and has a place on the line.
Two separate digits are not a part of a whole.

vocabulary.definition: A number with a dot, like 0.5, that shows a part less than one.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número con un punto, como 0.5, que muestra una parte menor que uno.
vocabulary.visual: 0.5 = 1/2 (halfway between 0 and 1 on the number line)
vocabulary.cloze: A number that uses a point to show parts of a whole is a ___.

examples.why: The decimal part places it between two integers.
Dropping the point changes the value entirely.

vocabulary.definition: A straight line where numbers are placed in order; numbers get smaller to the left and larger to the right.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una recta donde los números se colocan en orden; los números son menores a la izquierda y mayores a la derecha.
vocabulary.cloze: A line with numbers in order used to place and compare values is a ___.

examples.text: A line with -3, 0 and 3 marked in order
examples.why: Values placed in order, left to right, around 0.

examples.text: Three numbers listed in a column
examples.why: A list has no positions, so it shows no order or distance.

vocabulary.definition: Having the same value, just written a different way.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Tener el mismo valor, escrito de otra forma.
vocabulary.visual: 1/2 = 0.5 = 2/4 — all name the same point on the number line
vocabulary.cloze: Numbers that name the same value, like 1/2 and 0.5, are ___.

examples.why: The same point on the number line, written two ways.
One is ten times the other, so they land in different places.

vocabulary.definition: Whole numbers and their opposites, like -2, -1, 0, 1, 2.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Números enteros y sus opuestos, como -2, -1, 0, 1, 2.
vocabulary.cloze: A whole number or its opposite is an ___.

examples.why: Whole numbers, their opposites, and zero.
A number between two whole numbers is not an integer.

launch.narrative: Captain Vega's advanced treasure map uses precise coordinates — not just whole numbers! One clue says the treasure is at -2.5 on the map (halfway between -2 and -3). Another clue points to 3/4 of the way from 0 to 1. A third clue leads to -1 1/2. To find each treasure, you must plot these exact rational numbers on the number line.

conceptIntro.heading: How do you place rational numbers on a number line?
conceptIntro.intro: A rational number is any number you can write as a fraction. This includes fractions, decimals, and integers. Many rational numbers fall between two whole numbers.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: To plot a rational number, find the two whole numbers it falls between, then split the space into equal parts.

iDo.title: Watch me
lines: I will plot -2.5 on the number line.
First, the whole numbers it falls between: -2.5 is between -2 and -3.
The .5 means halfway, so I split the space between -2 and -3 in half.
I place my dot exactly halfway between -2 and -3. That is -2.5.

weDo.title: Let's try together
lines: Now let's plot 0.75. Which two whole numbers is it between? It is between 0 and 1.
What does 0.75 mean? It is 3/4 of the way from 0 to 1.
So we split 0 to 1 into 4 equal parts and place the dot at the 3rd mark.

youDo.title: Now it's your turn
lines: In the explore, plot each treasure clue like -2.5, 0.75, and -1.5 at its exact spot on the number line.

explore.instructions: Plot each rational number at its precise location on the number line.
explore.label: Plot each treasure clue at its exact location on the number line.

discourse.prompt: How did you decide exactly where to place rational numbers that fall between whole numbers?
discourse.sentenceFrame: To plot ___, I found the whole numbers it falls between, which are ___ and ___. Then I estimated ___ of the way between them because ___.

diagram.title: Between the Whole Numbers
diagram.caption: Every tick is one half. Drag each number to its exact spot — halves sit between the whole numbers, not on them.

diagram.intro: Drag the point to a rational number (halves). See its distance from zero and its opposite.

optional.stem: The first trail marker sits between 0 and 1. Which rational number belongs there?
optional.explanation: 3/4 = 0.75, which lands between 0 and 1. 1.5 and 2 are larger, and -1/2 is to the left of 0.
choiceFeedback: 1.5 is one and a half, which lands past 1. The marker needs a number smaller than one whole.
The negative sign puts this marker to the left of 0, not between 0 and 1.
This value is a full 2 units from 0, which lands past 1. You need a number smaller than one whole.
optional.stemEs: El primer marcador del sendero está entre 0 y 1. ¿Qué número racional corresponde ahí?
optional.explanationEs: 3/4 = 0.75, que cae entre 0 y 1. 1.5 y 2 son mayores, y -1/2 está a la izquierda de 0.
hints: Numbers between 0 and 1 are positive but smaller than one whole.
Convert each option to a decimal so it is easy to compare against 0 and 1.
Check the sign of each option first and rule out the negative one. Then convert what is left to decimals and keep the value that lands below 1.
hintsEs: Los números entre 0 y 1 son positivos pero menores que un entero.
Convierte cada opción a decimal para compararla fácilmente con 0 y 1.
Revisa primero el signo de cada opción y descarta la negativa. Luego convierte las demás a decimales y quédate con el valor que quede por debajo de 1.

optional.stem: Order these three trail markers from least to greatest: -1.5, 0.5, -0.5.
optional.explanation: The farthest left on the number line comes first: -1.5, then -0.5, then 0.5.
choiceFeedback: That is greatest to least. The question asks for least first.
The two negatives are swapped. Between -0.5 and -1.5, the one farther from 0 sits farther left and is therefore the smaller value.
This list starts correctly but then jumps over a negative. Every negative number comes before every positive one when you order least to greatest.
optional.stemEs: Ordena estos tres marcadores del sendero de menor a mayor: -1.5, 0.5, -0.5.
optional.explanationEs: El que está más a la izquierda en la recta numérica va primero: -1.5, luego -0.5 y después 0.5.
hints: Least to greatest means left to right on the number line.
Split the markers into negatives and positives first — every negative is less than every positive.
Among the negatives, -1.5 is farther from 0 than -0.5, so it sits farther left. Place those two in order, then add the positive marker.
hintsEs: De menor a mayor significa de izquierda a derecha en la recta numérica.
Separa primero los marcadores en negativos y positivos: todo negativo es menor que todo positivo.
Entre los negativos, -1.5 está más lejos de 0 que -0.5, así que queda más a la izquierda. Coloca esos dos en orden y luego agrega el marcador positivo.

optional.stem: On the trail map, -3/4 sits to the LEFT of which marker?
optional.explanation: -3/4 = -0.75 and -1/4 = -0.25. Since -0.75 is farther left (less), -3/4 is to the left of -1/4.
choiceFeedback: -1 sits farther left than -3/4 (because -1 < -0.75), so -3/4 comes AFTER it, not before. You need a marker -3/4 sits to the left of.
This marker is much farther from 0 than -3/4 is, so it sits to the left rather than the right. Compare the decimal values.
-7/8 is -0.875, which is farther left than -3/4. You are looking for a marker that -3/4 comes before.
optional.stemEs: En el mapa del sendero, -3/4 está a la IZQUIERDA de ¿cuál marcador?
optional.explanationEs: -3/4 = -0.75 y -1/4 = -0.25. Como -0.75 está más a la izquierda (es menor), -3/4 está a la izquierda de -1/4.
hints: Being to the left on a number line means being the smaller number.
Convert every marker to a decimal so you can compare them directly.
-3/4 is -0.75. Convert each option to a decimal and look for the one that is greater than -0.75, since that marker sits to the right.
hintsEs: Estar a la izquierda en una recta numérica significa ser el número menor.
Convierte cada marcador a decimal para poder compararlos directamente.
-3/4 es -0.75. Convierte cada opción a decimal y busca la que sea mayor que -0.75, porque ese marcador queda a la derecha.

optional.label: Match each decimal trail marker to its equal fraction.
optional.explanation: Read each decimal by its place value and write that as a fraction: 0.5 is five tenths, which simplifies to 1/2; 0.25 is twenty-five hundredths, which simplifies to 1/4; 0.2 is two tenths, which simplifies to 1/5; and −0.5 keeps its sign, giving −1/2. The negative marker can only pair with the negative fraction, so that match is settled by the sign alone.
optional.explanationEs: Lee cada decimal por su valor posicional y escríbelo como fracción: 0.5 son cinco décimos, que se simplifica a 1/2; 0.25 son veinticinco centésimos, que se simplifica a 1/4; 0.2 son dos décimos, que se simplifica a 1/5; y −0.5 conserva su signo, lo que da −1/2. El marcador negativo solo puede emparejarse con la fracción negativa, así que ese par se resuelve solo con el signo.
optional.labelEs: Une cada marcador decimal del sendero con su fracción equivalente.

optional.instructions: Sort each trail marker by whether it sits to the LEFT of 0 or to the RIGHT of 0 on the number line.
optional.explanation: Only the sign matters here, not the size. −0.75, −2.5, and −1 1/2 all carry a negative sign, so they sit to the left of 0. The markers 1/4, 0.6, and 3/4 have no negative sign, so they sit to the right of 0. You never need to convert or compare the values — −2.5 is much farther from zero than −0.75, but both land on the same side.
optional.explanationEs: Aquí solo importa el signo, no el tamaño. −0.75, −2.5 y −1 1/2 llevan signo negativo, así que quedan a la izquierda de 0. Los marcadores 1/4, 0.6 y 3/4 no tienen signo negativo, así que quedan a la derecha de 0. No hace falta convertir ni comparar los valores: −2.5 está mucho más lejos del cero que −0.75, pero ambos caen del mismo lado.
optional.instructionsEs: Clasifica cada marcador del sendero según si queda a la IZQUIERDA del 0 o a la DERECHA del 0 en la recta numérica.

optional.title: Level 2 Extension — The Mismarked Trail Post

workedExample.label: Problem
workedExample.work: Place -3/4 and -1/4 on the trail, then decide which marker is greater.
workedExample.workEs: Coloca -3/4 y -1/4 en el sendero, y decide cuál marcador es mayor.

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: -3/4 has a 3 on top and -1/4 has a 1 on top. A bigger numerator means a bigger number, so -3/4 is greater.
workedExample.workEs: -3/4 tiene un 3 arriba y -1/4 tiene un 1 arriba. Un numerador mayor significa un número mayor, así que -3/4 es mayor.

workedExample.label: Student answer
workedExample.work: -3/4 is plotted to the RIGHT of -1/4 and called the greater value.
workedExample.workEs: -3/4 queda graficado a la DERECHA de -1/4 y se declara el valor mayor.

optional.correctWork: For negative numbers, a bigger numerator does NOT mean a bigger value. -3/4 = -0.75 and -1/4 = -0.25. On the number line, -3/4 is farther LEFT than -1/4, so -3/4 is actually LESS than -1/4. The marker -3/4 should be plotted to the left of -1/4, and -1/4 is the greater value.
hints: Turn each fraction into a decimal: what is -3/4 and what is -1/4?
On a number line, the value farther to the left is always less, even when the numerator looks bigger.
optional.titleEs: Extensión de Nivel 2 — El poste del sendero mal marcado
optional.explanation: The "Student thinking" step applies a rule for positive fractions to negative ones. As decimals, −3/4 = −0.75 and −1/4 = −0.25, so −3/4 lies farther left on the number line and is the smaller value. A larger numerator moves a negative fraction farther from zero, which makes it less, so −1/4 is the greater marker and −3/4 belongs to its left.
optional.explanationEs: El paso "Student thinking" aplica a los negativos una regla que solo sirve para fracciones positivas. Como decimales, −3/4 = −0.75 y −1/4 = −0.25, así que −3/4 queda más a la izquierda en la recta numérica y es el valor menor. Un numerador mayor aleja del cero a una fracción negativa, lo que la hace menor, así que −1/4 es el marcador mayor y −3/4 va a su izquierda.
optional.correctWorkEs: Con números negativos, un numerador mayor NO significa un valor mayor. -3/4 = -0.75 y -1/4 = -0.25. En la recta numérica, -3/4 está más a la IZQUIERDA que -1/4, así que -3/4 es MENOR que -1/4. El marcador -3/4 debe graficarse a la izquierda de -1/4, y -1/4 es el valor mayor.

approaching.stem: Which point is located between -1 and -2 on the number line?
approaching.explanation: -1.5 is between -1 and -2 because it is 0.5 units to the left of -1 (or 0.5 units to the right of -2).
choiceFeedback: -0.5 sits between 0 and -1 — it has not traveled past -1 yet. You need a number that lands beyond -1 but before -2.
This value is farther left than -2, so it lands between -2 and -3. Look for a number just past -1 heading toward -2.
That value is positive, which puts it on the right side of 0. Both -1 and -2 sit to the left of 0, so the number you need is negative.
hints: 'Between -1 and -2' is on the NEGATIVE side, in the gap from -1 to -2.
Turn each choice into a spot on the number line and check: is it past -1 but not past -2?
Start at -1 and move half a unit farther left. Which choice lands in that gap between -1 and -2?
approaching.stemEs: ¿Qué punto está ubicado entre -1 y -2 en la recta numérica?
approaching.explanationEs: -1.5 está entre -1 y -2 porque queda 0.5 unidades a la izquierda de -1 (o 0.5 unidades a la derecha de -2).
hintsEs: 'Entre −1 y −2' está del lado NEGATIVO, en el espacio de −1 a −2.
Convierte cada opción en un punto de la recta numérica y revisa: ¿pasa de −1 pero no pasa de −2?
Empieza en −1 y muévete media unidad más a la izquierda. ¿Qué opción cae en ese espacio entre −1 y −2?

choiceFeedback: Not quite. 0.25 means 25 hundredths = 25/100 = ___.
This fraction equals 0.4 as a decimal, which is larger than 0.25. Write 0.25 as a fraction over 100 first, then simplify.
This fraction is about 0.333, so it is bigger than 0.25. Convert the decimal into hundredths and reduce that fraction.
hints: Read 0.25 as a place-value number: 25 hundredths.
Write it as 25/100, then simplify by dividing the top and bottom by the same number.
Divide both 25 and 100 by 25. What simpler fraction do you get?
hintsEs: Lee 0.25 como un número con valor posicional: 25 centésimas.
Escríbelo como 25/100 y luego simplifica dividiendo arriba y abajo entre el mismo número.
Divide 25 y 100 entre 25. ¿Qué fracción más simple obtienes?

approaching.label: Match each fraction to its decimal equivalent.
hints: Each fraction equals a decimal. Halves, quarters, fifths, and tenths all have decimal partners you know.
Divide top by bottom and keep the sign: -3/4 stays negative. For mixed numbers, keep the whole part and convert the fraction.
Start with 1/2: 1 ÷ 2 = 0.5 — match those two. Now convert 3/10 by reading it as 'three tenths.'
approaching.explanation: Dividing the numerator by the denominator converts each fraction, and the sign never changes: 1/2 = 0.5, −3/4 = −0.75, 3/10 = 0.3, and −1/5 = −0.2. For the mixed numbers, keep the whole part and convert only the fraction, so 1 1/4 = 1.25 and −2 1/2 = −2.5. Matching the signs first splits the cards into two smaller groups before you compute.
approaching.explanationEs: Dividir el numerador entre el denominador convierte cada fracción, y el signo nunca cambia: 1/2 = 0.5, −3/4 = −0.75, 3/10 = 0.3 y −1/5 = −0.2. Para los números mixtos, conserva la parte entera y convierte solo la fracción, así que 1 1/4 = 1.25 y −2 1/2 = −2.5. Emparejar primero los signos divide las tarjetas en dos grupos más pequeños antes de calcular.
approaching.labelEs: Une cada fracción con su decimal equivalente.
hintsEs: Cada fracción es igual a un decimal. Los medios, cuartos, quintos y décimos tienen decimales que ya conoces.
Divide arriba entre abajo y conserva el signo: −3/4 sigue siendo negativo. En los números mixtos, conserva la parte entera y convierte la fracción.
Empieza con 1/2: 1 ÷ 2 = 0.5 — únelos. Ahora convierte 3/10 leyéndolo como 'tres décimos'.

approaching.stem: Where is -3/4 located on the number line?
approaching.explanation: -3/4 = -0.75, which is between 0 and -1. It is 3/4 of the way from 0 toward -1.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. -3/4 = -0.75, which is between ___ and ___.
-3/4 is less than one whole unit away from 0, so it never even reaches -1. Convert the fraction to a decimal and see how far left it travels.
The distance is right, but the negative sign puts this number to the left of 0, not to the right.
hints: The size of -3/4 is less than 1 whole — its distance from zero is under 1.
Convert: 3/4 = 0.75, so -3/4 = -0.75. Now ask which two numbers -0.75 sits between on the line.
Start at 0 and move 0.75 units LEFT. Did you pass -1 on the way, or not?
approaching.stemEs: ¿Dónde se ubica -3/4 en la recta numérica?
approaching.explanationEs: -3/4 = -0.75, que está entre 0 y -1. Queda a 3/4 del camino de 0 hacia -1.
hintsEs: El tamaño de −3/4 es menor que 1 entero: su distancia desde cero es menor que 1.
Convierte: 3/4 = 0.75, así que −3/4 = −0.75. Ahora pregunta entre qué dos números queda −0.75 en la recta.
Empieza en 0 y muévete 0.75 unidades a la IZQUIERDA. ¿Pasaste el −1 en el camino o no?

approaching.label: Plot these rational numbers: -1, 0.5, -0.5, 1, -1.5
hints: The tick marks count by 0.5 — each hop is a HALF, not a whole unit.
For -1.5: go to -1 first, then one more half-tick left. Positives work the same way to the right.
Plot -1 and 1 on their whole-number ticks first. Then place 0.5 exactly halfway between 0 and 1.
approaching.explanation: The ticks step by 0.5, so each hop is half a unit. Place −1 and 1 on their whole-number ticks, then 0.5 one tick right of 0 and −0.5 one tick left of 0. For −1.5, go to −1 and take one more half-step left, landing between −1 and −2. Negative numbers move left of zero and positive numbers move right, so the two halves mirror each other across 0.
approaching.explanationEs: Las marcas avanzan de 0.5 en 0.5, así que cada salto es media unidad. Coloca −1 y 1 en sus marcas de números enteros, luego 0.5 una marca a la derecha de 0 y −0.5 una marca a la izquierda de 0. Para −1.5, ve a −1 y da otro medio paso a la izquierda, quedando entre −1 y −2. Los números negativos van a la izquierda del cero y los positivos a la derecha, así que las dos mitades se reflejan a través del 0.

approaching.title: Spot the Mistake: Plotting 1.5

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: 1.5 has a 1 and a 5, so I will plot it between 1 and 5.
workedExample.workEs: 1.5 tiene un 1 y un 5, así que lo graficaré entre 1 y 5.

workedExample.label: Student answer
workedExample.work: Point plotted at about 3, halfway between 1 and 5.
workedExample.workEs: Punto graficado cerca del 3, a la mitad entre 1 y 5.

approaching.correctWork: 1.5 does NOT mean between 1 and 5. The .5 is one half, so 1.5 is halfway between 1 and 2. I find the two whole numbers it falls between (1 and 2), split that space in half, and place the dot at the middle. The point belongs at 1.5, not 3.
hints: What does the .5 in 1.5 mean — is it a separate whole number or a part of one?
Which two whole numbers is 1.5 between? Split that space into equal parts.
approaching.explanation: The "Student thinking" step reads 1.5 as two separate whole numbers, 1 and 5. The digit after the decimal point names a part of one unit, not a second endpoint: .5 is one half. So 1.5 sits between the whole numbers 1 and 2, exactly halfway, not near 3.
approaching.explanationEs: El paso "Student thinking" lee 1.5 como dos números enteros separados, 1 y 5. La cifra después del punto decimal nombra una parte de una unidad, no un segundo extremo: .5 es un medio. Así que 1.5 queda entre los números enteros 1 y 2, justo a la mitad, no cerca del 3.
approaching.correctWorkEs: 1.5 NO significa entre 1 y 5. El .5 es un medio, así que 1.5 está a la mitad entre 1 y 2. Encuentro los dos números enteros entre los que cae (1 y 2), parto ese espacio a la mitad y coloco el punto en medio. El punto va en 1.5, no en 3.

onLevel.label: Plot these rational numbers: -3.5, -1/4, 2.75, -2, 1 1/2
hints: Mixed forms here — turn every number into a decimal first: -1/4 and 1 1/2 both need converting.
-1/4 = -0.25 and 1 1/2 = 1.5. Then place each one: whole part first, then the extra fraction of a unit.
Plot A at -3.5: go to -3, then half a tick farther left. Then plot D at -2, right on its whole-number tick.
onLevel.explanation: Convert every value to a decimal first: −1/4 = −0.25 and 1 1/2 = 1.5. Then A goes half a step left of −3 at −3.5, D lands right on the −2 tick, E lands on the 1.5 tick, C sits at 2.75 — three quarters of the way from 2 to 3, just past the 2.5 tick — and B sits at −0.25, only a quarter of a unit left of zero.
onLevel.explanationEs: Convierte primero cada valor a decimal: −1/4 = −0.25 y 1 1/2 = 1.5. Luego A va medio paso a la izquierda de −3, en −3.5; D cae justo en la marca de −2; E cae en la marca de 1.5; C está en 2.75, a tres cuartos del camino de 2 a 3, apenas pasando la marca de 2.5; y B está en −0.25, a solo un cuarto de unidad a la izquierda del cero.

onLevel.instructions: Convert between fraction and decimal form. Then plot on a mental number line to compare.
onLevel.hint: Convert between fraction and decimal, then name the two integers each value falls between.
hints: Each row needs the same number in two forms, plus the two integers it sits between.
Fraction to decimal: divide top by bottom. Decimal to fraction: use place value (0.6 = six tenths). Keep negatives negative.
Row 1: divide 3 by 4 to get the decimal. Then ask: is that result more than 0 and less than 1?
onLevel.explanation: Convert each value, then name the integers on either side of it. 3/4 = 0.75, between 0 and 1. −7/2 = −3.5, between −4 and −3, since more negative means farther left. 0.6 is six tenths, which is 3/5, between 0 and 1. −1.25 is −1 1/4, between −2 and −1. And 2 1/5 = 2.2, between 2 and 3. For negatives, the integer with the larger absolute value is the one on the left.
onLevel.explanationEs: Convierte cada valor y luego nombra los enteros que lo rodean. 3/4 = 0.75, entre 0 y 1. −7/2 = −3.5, entre −4 y −3, ya que más negativo significa más a la izquierda. 0.6 son seis décimos, o sea 3/5, entre 0 y 1. −1.25 es −1 1/4, entre −2 y −1. Y 2 1/5 = 2.2, entre 2 y 3. Para los negativos, el entero con mayor valor absoluto es el que queda a la izquierda.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Convierte entre la forma de fracción y de decimal. Después ubícalos mentalmente en una recta numérica para compararlos.
hintsEs: Cada fila necesita el mismo número en dos formas, más los dos enteros entre los que queda.
Fracción a decimal: divide arriba entre abajo. Decimal a fracción: usa el valor posicional (0.6 = seis décimos). Conserva los negativos.
Fila 1: divide 3 entre 4 para obtener el decimal. Luego pregunta: ¿ese resultado es más que 0 y menos que 1?

onLevel.label: Order these rational numbers from LEAST to GREATEST.
hints: This is a mix of fractions and decimals — convert them all to decimals so they're easy to compare.
-1/4 = -0.25 and 1/2 = 0.5. Then order like a number line: most negative first, then up through the positives.
Compare the negatives first: -2.5, -1.5, and -0.25. The one farthest below zero starts the list.
onLevel.explanation: Convert the fractions so everything is in the same form: −1/4 = −0.25 and 1/2 = 0.5. Reading left to right on a number line gives −2.5, −1.5, −1/4, 1/2, 0.75, 3. Among the negatives, −2.5 is farthest from zero so it is the least — the opposite of how the numbers would order if they were positive.
onLevel.explanationEs: Convierte las fracciones para que todo quede en la misma forma: −1/4 = −0.25 y 1/2 = 0.5. Al leer de izquierda a derecha en la recta numérica queda −2.5, −1.5, −1/4, 1/2, 0.75, 3. Entre los negativos, −2.5 es el más alejado del cero, así que es el menor, lo contrario de cómo se ordenarían si fueran positivos.
onLevel.labelEs: Ordena estos números racionales del MENOR al MAYOR.
hintsEs: Aquí hay una mezcla de fracciones y decimales: conviértelos todos a decimales para compararlos fácil.
−1/4 = −0.25 y 1/2 = 0.5. Luego ordena como en una recta numérica: el más negativo primero y luego hacia los positivos.
Compara primero los negativos: −2.5, −1.5 y −0.25. El que está más abajo de cero empieza la lista.

onLevel.stem: Which rational number is closest to 0 on the number line?
onLevel.explanation: |-1/4| = 0.25, |0.5| = 0.5, |-2| = 2, |1.75| = 1.75. Since 0.25 is the smallest absolute value, -1/4 is closest to zero.
choiceFeedback: |0.5| = 0.5, but one negative option sits even closer to zero than that. Distance ignores sign — compare absolute values before ruling out the negatives.
Distance from 0 is what matters here, and this number sits a full 2 units away. Compare absolute values rather than signs.
This value is almost 2 units from 0. Convert every option to a decimal and compare how far each one is from zero, ignoring direction.
hints: 'Closest to 0' means the SMALLEST distance from zero — the sign doesn't matter.
Find each choice's absolute value — for example |0.5| = 0.5 — then look for the smallest distance.
Write every choice as a distance from zero, then compare all four distances and take the smallest.
onLevel.stemEs: ¿Qué número racional está más cerca de 0 en la recta numérica?
onLevel.explanationEs: |-1/4| = 0.25, |0.5| = 0.5, |-2| = 2, |1.75| = 1.75. Como 0.25 es el valor absoluto más pequeño, -1/4 es el más cercano a cero.
hintsEs: 'Más cerca de 0' significa la MENOR distancia desde cero; el signo no importa.
Halla el valor absoluto de cada opción (convierte −1/4 en 0.25 y así) y luego busca la distancia menor.
Empieza con dos: |−1/4| = 0.25 y |0.5| = 0.5. Halla las otras dos distancias y compara las cuatro.

onLevel.title: Spot the Mistake: Plotting -2.25

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: It is negative, so I go past -2. The .25 is one quarter, so I count toward 0 (to the right) by a quarter unit and land between -2 and -1.
workedExample.workEs: Es negativo, así que paso el -2. El .25 es un cuarto, así que cuento hacia el 0 (a la derecha) un cuarto de unidad y caigo entre -2 y -1.

onLevel.correctWork: Going more negative means moving LEFT, not right. -2.25 is between -2 and -3 (it is a quarter of a unit to the LEFT of -2), not between -2 and -1. I split the space from -2 to -3 into 4 equal parts and place the dot at the first mark past -2, at -2.25.
hints: On a number line, which direction is 'more negative' — left or right?
Which two whole numbers is -2.25 between? It is just past -2 heading toward -3.
onLevel.explanation: The "Student thinking" step moves right from −2, back toward zero, which makes the number less negative instead of more. The extra .25 has to be added to the negative direction, so −2.25 sits a quarter of a unit to the left of −2, between −2 and −3. Splitting that space into 4 equal parts and marking the first one past −2 puts the dot in the right place.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso "Student thinking" se mueve a la derecha desde −2, de regreso hacia el cero, lo que hace el número menos negativo en lugar de más. El .25 adicional debe sumarse en la dirección negativa, así que −2.25 queda a un cuarto de unidad a la izquierda de −2, entre −2 y −3. Dividir ese espacio en 4 partes iguales y marcar la primera después de −2 coloca el punto en el lugar correcto.
onLevel.correctWorkEs: Hacerse más negativo significa moverse a la IZQUIERDA, no a la derecha. -2.25 está entre -2 y -3 (un cuarto de unidad a la IZQUIERDA de -2), no entre -2 y -1. Parto el espacio de -2 a -3 en 4 partes iguales y coloco el punto en la primera marca después de -2, en -2.25.

onLevel.stem: Which number is farthest to the LEFT on a number line?
onLevel.explanation: Farther left means more negative: -4 < -1 < 0 < 2, so -4 is farthest left.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Farther left means more negative: ___ < -1 < 0 < 2, so ___ is farthest left.
Zero is the dividing point, not the far left end. Every negative number sits to the left of it.
Positive numbers sit to the right of 0, so this is the wrong direction. Farther left means more negative.
hints: Farthest LEFT means the least value — the most negative number.
Sketch the line: negatives sit left of 0, and among negatives, a bigger distance from zero is farther left.
Place -1 and -4 on the line: count how far below zero each one sits. Which is farther out?
onLevel.stemEs: ¿Qué número está más a la IZQUIERDA en una recta numérica?
onLevel.explanationEs: Estar más a la izquierda significa ser más negativo: -4 < -1 < 0 < 2, así que -4 está más a la izquierda.
hintsEs: Lo más a la IZQUIERDA significa el valor menor: el número más negativo.
Dibuja la recta: los negativos van a la izquierda de 0, y entre negativos, una mayor distancia desde cero queda más a la izquierda.
Coloca −1 y −4 en la recta: cuenta qué tan abajo de cero está cada uno. ¿Cuál queda más lejos?

onLevel.explanation: The opposite of a number is its reflection across 0, so the opposite of -3/4 is 3/4.
choiceFeedback: -3/4 is the number itself, unchanged. An opposite reflects across 0 — same distance, other side — so the sign has to switch.
Flipping the numerator and denominator gives a reciprocal, not an opposite. An opposite keeps the same distance from 0 and changes only the direction.
Zero is its own opposite and sits at the center. The opposite of a number is the same distance from 0, just on the other side.
hints: 'Opposite' means the mirror image across zero — same distance, other side.
Keep the size 3/4 the same and flip the sign. (Don't flip the fraction upside down — that's a reciprocal.)
-3/4 sits 3/4 of a unit LEFT of zero. Mark the point the same distance on the RIGHT — that's its opposite.
onLevel.explanationEs: El opuesto de un número es su reflejo respecto a 0, así que el opuesto de -3/4 es 3/4.

extending.title: Find the Plotting Error

workedExample.label: Student thinking
workedExample.work: -3/4 has a 3 and a 4, so I go to -3 on the number line and then count 4 more to the left
workedExample.workEs: -3/4 tiene un 3 y un 4, así que voy al -3 en la recta y luego cuento 4 más a la izquierda

extending.correctWork: -3/4 means negative three-fourths, which is 3/4 of the way from 0 toward -1. It should be plotted between 0 and -1, not at -7. The student treated the numerator and denominator as separate whole numbers.
hints: What does the fraction 3/4 actually mean? How much of a whole is it?
-3/4 is a number between 0 and -1. It is 3/4 of one unit to the left of zero.
extending.explanation: The "Student thinking" step splits −3/4 into the whole numbers 3 and 4 instead of reading it as one value. The bar in a fraction means division, so −3/4 is three fourths of a single unit taken in the negative direction: it belongs between 0 and −1, three quarters of the way to −1. A fraction whose numerator is smaller than its denominator can never reach even one whole unit, let alone −7.
extending.explanationEs: El paso "Student thinking" separa −3/4 en los números enteros 3 y 4 en lugar de leerlo como un solo valor. La barra de una fracción significa división, así que −3/4 son tres cuartos de una sola unidad tomados en dirección negativa: queda entre 0 y −1, a tres cuartos del camino hacia −1. Una fracción cuyo numerador es menor que su denominador nunca puede alcanzar ni siquiera una unidad completa, mucho menos −7.
extending.correctWorkEs: -3/4 significa tres cuartos negativos, que es 3/4 del camino de 0 hacia -1. Debe graficarse entre 0 y -1, no en -7. El estudiante trató el numerador y el denominador como números enteros separados.

extending.prompt: Name three different rational numbers between -1 and 0. Write each as both a fraction and a decimal. Explain how you know they are between -1 and 0.
extending.sentenceFrame: Three rational numbers between -1 and 0 are: ___ = ___, ___ = ___, and ___ = ___. I know they are between -1 and 0 because ___.
extending.hint: Use examples with specific coordinates to explain your thinking.
hints: You need numbers that are negative but greater than -1 — think of small negative fractions.
Pick easy fractions like halves, fourths, or tenths, make them negative, and write each one's decimal twin.
Test -1/2: as a decimal it's -0.5, which is left of 0 but right of -1 — so it works. Find two more like it.
extending.explanation: Any negative number greater than −1 works, so pick friendly fractions and convert them: −1/2 = −0.5, −1/4 = −0.25, and −3/10 = −0.3. Each is negative, so it sits left of 0, but each has an absolute value less than 1, so it never reaches −1. On the number line all three land inside the single unit between −1 and 0.
extending.explanationEs: Sirve cualquier número negativo mayor que −1, así que elige fracciones fáciles y conviértelas: −1/2 = −0.5, −1/4 = −0.25 y −3/10 = −0.3. Cada uno es negativo, así que queda a la izquierda de 0, pero cada uno tiene un valor absoluto menor que 1, así que nunca llega a −1. En la recta numérica los tres caen dentro de la única unidad que va de −1 a 0.
extending.promptEs: Nombra tres números racionales diferentes entre -1 y 0. Escribe cada uno como fracción y como decimal. Explica cómo sabes que están entre -1 y 0.
hintsEs: Necesitas números que sean negativos pero mayores que −1: piensa en fracciones negativas pequeñas.
Escoge fracciones fáciles como medios, cuartos o décimos, hazlas negativas y escribe el decimal gemelo de cada una.
Prueba −1/2: como decimal es −0.5, que está a la izquierda de 0 pero a la derecha de −1, así que sirve. Halla dos más como esa.

extending.label: Which side is greater? Compare -2/3 and -3/4.
extending.instructions: Convert to decimals: -2/3 ≈ -0.667 and -3/4 = -0.75. Since -0.667 is closer to zero, -2/3 > -3/4. The left side is greater.
hints: Both numbers are negative, so the GREATER one is the one closer to zero.
Convert both fractions to decimals with the same number of places, then compare their distances from zero.
Start with the right side: -3/4 = -0.75. Now convert -2/3 to a decimal and check which sits closer to 0.
extending.explanation: Convert both to decimals: −2/3 ≈ −0.667 and −3/4 = −0.75. Because both are negative, the one closer to zero is the greater one, and −0.667 sits to the right of −0.75 on the number line. So −2/3 > −3/4 and the left side of the scale is greater, even though 3/4 would beat 2/3 if both were positive.
extending.explanationEs: Convierte ambos a decimales: −2/3 ≈ −0.667 y −3/4 = −0.75. Como los dos son negativos, el que está más cerca del cero es el mayor, y −0.667 queda a la derecha de −0.75 en la recta numérica. Así que −2/3 > −3/4 y el lado izquierdo de la balanza es mayor, aunque 3/4 le ganaría a 2/3 si ambos fueran positivos.

extending.stem: On a number line, point P is located at -2.5. Which statement describes its location best?
choiceFeedback: Not quite. -2.5 sits exactly halfway between ___ and ___.
The distance is right, but the sign got dropped. A negative value sits on the left side of 0.
-2.5 has not traveled all the way to -3. The .5 means it stops partway between two whole numbers.
hints: The .5 in -2.5 means half a unit MORE negative than -2.
Start at -2 on the number line and move another half unit left. Describe where you land relative to -2 and -3.
Mark -2 and -3, then place -2.5. Is it nearer to -2, nearer to -3, or exactly in the middle of them?
extending.stemEs: En una recta numérica, el punto P está ubicado en -2.5. ¿Qué enunciado describe mejor su ubicación?
extending.explanationEs: -2.5 queda exactamente a la mitad entre -2 y -3.
hintsEs: El .5 de −2.5 significa media unidad MÁS negativa que −2.
Empieza en −2 en la recta numérica y muévete otra media unidad a la izquierda. Describe dónde caes respecto a −2 y −3.
Marca −2 y −3 y luego coloca −2.5. ¿Está más cerca de −2, más cerca de −3, o exactamente en medio?

extending.stem: Which list of numbers is ordered from LEAST to GREATEST?
extending.explanation: Least to greatest runs most-negative to most-positive: -5, -2, 0, 3.
choiceFeedback: Not quite. Least to greatest runs most-negative to most-positive: ___.
The two negatives are out of order here. Among negative numbers, the one with the larger digit sits farther left, which makes it the smaller value.
This list jumps back and forth across 0. Least to greatest has to move steadily left to right along the number line.
hints: Least to greatest starts at the MOST negative number and climbs toward the positives.
Check each list: negatives must come first (farthest below zero leading), then 0, then the positives.
Compare -5 and -2 on a number line: which is farther below zero? The correct list starts with that number.
extending.stemEs: ¿Qué lista de números está ordenada de MENOR a MAYOR?
extending.explanationEs: De menor a mayor va de lo más negativo a lo más positivo: -5, -2, 0, 3.
hintsEs: De menor a mayor empieza en el número MÁS negativo y sube hacia los positivos.
Revisa cada lista: los negativos deben ir primero (encabezando el más abajo de cero), luego 0 y luego los positivos.
Compara −5 y −2 en una recta numérica: ¿cuál está más abajo de cero? La lista correcta empieza con ese número.

optionalActivity.name: Rational Number Trail Markers
optionalActivity.intro: Follow Captain Vega's hiking trail and read each marker post to place every rational number at its exact spot.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Rational Numbers on the Number Line is treating the numerator and denominator of a negative fraction as two separate whole numbers instead of one value between two integers — for example, plotting -3/4 by going to -3 and then counting 4 more units to the left, landing (incorrectly) at -7, instead of recognizing that -3/4 = -0.75, which sits between 0 and -1. Before you submit an answer, find the two whole numbers your value falls between, then split that space into equal parts.

diagram.title: Water Level Against the Painted Mark
diagram.caption: 0 is the mark painted on the ramp. Drag each day's dot to its reading: above the mark is positive, below it is negative. The quarter-foot ticks are why −1.25 has a spot of its own.

connect.scenario: The boat ramp at Miller Lake has a full mark painted on it. When the water sits exactly on that mark, the ramp keeper writes 0 — the mark IS zero. Above the mark is positive, below it is negative. Last week she wrote: Monday +0.75 ft, Tuesday −1.25 ft, Wednesday −0.5 ft, Thursday +1.5 ft.
connect.promptQuestion: Put the four readings in order from lowest water to highest. How do the decimals let the keeper say something a whole number could not?
connect.prompt: The lowest reading was ___ and the highest was ___. Tuesday's ___ ft means the water sat 1¼ feet ___ the mark, which is between −1 and ___ on the number line.

check.stem: Where does −1.25 fall on the number line?
check.explanation: −1.25 is 1.25 units below zero — past −1, but not as far down as −2.

check.stem: Which day had the water level closest to the painted mark?
check.explanation: Compare absolute values: |−0.5| = 0.5 is the smallest distance from 0, so Wednesday was closest to the mark.

check.stem: Why are rational numbers more useful here than integers alone?
choices: They let the scientist record part-of-a-foot changes like 0.75 and −1.25
check.explanation: Integers would force every reading to a whole foot. Rational numbers — fractions and decimals — capture the in-between values, so the readings are far more precise.

connect.modelAnswer: Ordered from lowest to highest: Tuesday −1.25, Wednesday −0.5, Monday +0.75, Thursday +1.5. Tuesday's −1.25 ft means the water sat 1¼ feet BELOW the painted mark — past −1 but not as far down as −2. With whole feet the keeper could only write 'about 1 foot below', and the quarter-foot of missing water would go unrecorded.

exitTicket.stem: Which rational number is located between -2 and -3 on the number line?
exitTicket.explanation: -2.75 is between -2 and -3 because it is 0.75 units to the left of -2. -1.5 is between -1 and -2, and -3.5 is between -3 and -4.
choiceFeedback: -1.5 is to the right of -2, not between -2 and -3.
-3.5 is past -3 — you need a value between -2 and -3.
2.5 is positive — look on the negative side.
hints: You need a number on the negative side, sitting in the gap between -2 and -3.
Turn each choice into a number-line position: does it sit past -2 but before -3? Check the signs first.
Start at -2 and move left toward -3. A value like negative-2-and-a-bit lands in the gap — test each choice.

questions.explanation: Opposites are the same distance from 0 on opposite sides, so the opposite of −6 is 6.

questions.stem: On a number line, which number is farther to the LEFT: −8 or −3?
questions.explanation: Numbers get smaller going left, and −8 is smaller than −3, so −8 sits farther left.
On a number line the least value is the one farthest left, which is −8.

questions.stem: A point sits 5 units to the LEFT of 0 on a number line. What number is it?
questions.explanation: Left of 0 means negative, and 5 units away makes it −5.

items.term: Rational Numbers on the Number Line
items.meaning: Every rational number has one exact spot on the number line
A number that shows part of a whole, like 3/4
A straight line where numbers are placed in order

copyPanel.rule: To plot a rational number, find the two whole numbers it falls between, then split the space into equal parts
